subject: Dedicated capacity sizing: concurrency, context length, and tiered discount structure
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@helios.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helios.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@helios.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: dedicated capacity sizing and commercial ask

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We scoped a rough expected traffic profile during the call but wanted to put it in writing so your team can recommend the right pool size and a target committed discount. High level:~
- Peak requests: 1,200 reqs/min (spiky; 10% of minutes hit this peak)
- Average request size: ~650 tokens in + 180 tokens out (we use a summarization+Q&A flow)
- Typical context lengths: 1,000 - 2,048 tokens; occasional 4k for long-session exports
- Concurrency: 220 concurrent user sessions at peak; each session issues ~1 request/sec when active
- Model family: prefer an Llama-derivative equivalent (8-bit / quantized path is OK)

Can you share a recommended GPU pool (instance types / count), throughput guarantee SLO, and an initial committed pricing band we can discuss with procurement? Also please include any assumptions about batching and KV cache benefits.

Appreciate it — Alex

---
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@helios.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity sizing and commercial ask

Alex —

Thanks, that profile is super helpful. A few clarifying items before we hand off to sizing:
- Is 1,200 reqs/min measured as completed requests or connection attempts?
- How long are the typical model generations (latency goal per request)? SLO target (p95) you want us to design to?
- Are you able to use a short-lived streaming approach for the longer sessions, or do you need full blocking generations?

Assuming 1,200 completed reqs/min with the concurrency numbers you gave and a 2-second average generation latency target, we can sketch an initial sizing+pricing proposal. I've looped in Ben for throughput math and Marissa for pricing/commit discounts. We'll produce a short proposal and attach a workbook so you can tweak parameters.

Next steps: I'll get a draft back to you by EOD tomorrow. If procurement wants, we can schedule a 30-min commit/discount call Thursday.

Best,
Priya

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@helios.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity sizing and commercial ask

Alex / team —

I ran a quick sizing run using these assumptions (we'll share the calcs in sizing_calcs.csv):
- Traffic model: Peak 1,200 reqs/min => 20 reqs/sec sustained during peak minutes
- Concurrency mapping: 220 concurrent sessions; active sessions at peak ~60% => ~132 active sessions
- Average tokens generated: 180 tokens out, 650 tokens in (context cached where possible)
- Target latency: p95 <= 2.0s for interactive flows
- Model: 13B Llama-derivative, 8-bit quantized inference (best fit for quality/cost)

Sizing result (recommendation):
- Instance choice: A100-40GB style (or equivalent Ampere-class GPU with good FP16/INT8 kernels)
- Pool footprint: 6 GPUs for base committed pool + 2 GPUs headroom burst (autoscale on demand)
  - Base pool estimated sustained throughput: ~3,000 tokens/sec per GPU (model-dependent)
  - Effective token capacity across 6 GPUs: ~18,000 tokens/sec
  - Request throughput headroom handles the 1,200 req/min peak while allowing batching benefits

Why this fits: with batching and our KV cache for session contexts, average per-request compute drops significantly for repeated context tokens. We expect >30% effective reduction in compute compared to cold-generation assumptions for these session-heavy flows.

Commercial sketch (committed reserved model):
- Option A: 12-month commit, 6-GPU pool reserved (flat-rate monthly) — recommended for predictable unit economics
  - List price equivalent: $X/month (see attached proposal)
  - Committed discount band: 20% off hosted list for 12-month; additional 5% if paid annually upfront or if commit expands to 8 GPUs within first 90 days
- Option B: 24-month commit, 6-GPU pool reserved + 2 guaranteed burst GPUs — deeper discount
  - Committed discount: 30% off hosted list equivalent; includes 2 guaranteed burst GPUs available up to 30% of peak minutes

SLOs we can support in Dedicated:
- Throughput guarantee: baseline sustained throughput for reserved pool corresponding to the GPU count (we can express as tokens/sec guaranteed)
- Latency SLO: p95 inference time target (depends on model & batch policy) — we can commit to p95 <=2.5s for the committed configuration; 2.0s is achievable with tuned batch windows during peak but we prefer to test in a short pilot

Assumptions & caveats:
- Model mix: if you swap to larger models (30B+), GPU count should increase or quantization applied
- Network egress and embedding heavy flows are priced separately
- We recommend a 2-week pilot with a small test pool (2 GPUs) to validate real-world batching and cache reuse before firm commit

Marissa, I left placeholders in the attached PDF for the pricing bands.

Ben

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@helios.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@helios.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity sizing and commercial ask

Hi Alex —

Attaching the formal draft (redwood_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf) and the editable workload workbook (helios_workload_profile_v3.xlsx). Key commercial points summarized below so procurement has a clean decision sheet:

Proposal highlights:
- Recommended committed configuration: 6x A100-class GPUs reserved (12-month) with up to 2x burst GPUs available for unpredictable spikes
- Pricing (examples):
  - 6-GPU reserved monthly: $165k/month list -> committed price tier 1: $132k/month (20% discount)
  - 6-GPU reserved (24-month): $115k/month effective (30% discount) + 2 guaranteed burst GPUs for up to 30% of peak minutes
  - Add-on: priority support & extended observability bundle at +$4k/month
- Credits & onboarding: 2-week pilot credit applied on first invoice if pilot metrics hit agreed thresholds
- SLA: 99.5% uptime on the serving plane for Dedicated; latency SLOs specified per model in appendix

Negotiation levers for procurement:
- Commit length (12 vs 24 months)
- GPU count floor (start at 6, scale to 8 to unlock extra discount)
- Payment terms (monthly vs annual prepay)
- Observability and retention add-ons (negotiable)

If procurement is interested, we can turn this into a redline-ready order form and DocuSign link.

Marissa

---
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@helios.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@helios.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity sizing and commercial ask

Team —

Thanks, this is clear and exactly what procurement needs. A couple quick asks before we move to PO:
1) Can you confirm the expected pilot metrics and the credit—what thresholds (latency & throughput) must we hit?
2) For the 24-month option, what is the process/timing to add 2 more GPUs if we commit to scale to 8 within 90 days?
3) Can you provide a one-page SLO summary we can attach to the contract (p95 target, availability, incident response)?

If those are straightforward I’ll route to procurement and we’ll aim to sign the 12-month option to start and take the 24-month off the table for internal approval; we may come back for the 24-month if usage grows faster than expected.

Appreciate the quick turn — Alex

[Attachments referenced: helios_workload_profile_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal), sizing_calcs.csv (calculation export)]
